scope: scripts/qualify_safety_changes.py on a frozen Debug build of 2d74ebb (D:/wp/b66, git-archived sources with source-manifest.json) under TIA Portal V21 Update 3 with an activated STEP 7 Safety license, in a fresh owned scratch with a CPU 1511F-1 PN whose generated scratch user holds ProtectionLevelFailsafeAccess (failsafeRuntimeAccess, owned scratch only) and an ET 200SP station with two F-DI 8x24VDC HF (66 steps): safety_import_xml now compiles every device instead of only the PLC software. The generated F-FBD block Main_Safety_RTG1 was re-imported with a filled comment text, with checkpoint, all-devices compile (device-path-v1 receipt, complete scope), save, change_status and an exact state diff limited to that block plus recorded F-compile side effects; every F-PLC block, including the F-compiler block DB1_C, read consistent right after the import (it read inconsistent after the earlier PLC-only compile, local.safety_import.20261028). A wrong previewHash was refused (PreviewMismatch), prepare refusals covered a missing acknowledgement, a scope mismatch and a standard block (SafetyBoundary), the import persisted across a fresh Portal reopen and a second import was restored from its checkpoint. The safety reads, printout and safety_fparameter_set passed again in the same run.
limitations: One generated F-FBD block (Main_Safety_RTG1) re-imported with a comment change; no F-logic behavior, F-I/O commissioning, acceptance, login, password or download.

The import compiles every device of the project, like safety_fparameter_set; a project with a device that cannot be compiled (for example a Startdrive drive, which exposes no device compile service) cannot apply it.
One F-CPU 1511F-1 PN with an ET 200SP station and two F-DI in an owned scratch; the fail-safe runtime right is granted to the scratch's generated user only.
